solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With thick coat on back, plays truant from school …

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for skipping lessons from end to start

parts.note: to cut a class is to skip it, so cuts means plays truant from
a coed is a co-educational school, one taking boys and girls

explanation.surface: A pupil wrapped in a heavy coat bunks off school, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal indicator. A coed is the American name for a co-educational school. The ellipsis links this clue to 6 across in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a thick plaster rendering, so a wall with that thick coat on it has been rendered this way.

clue.text: Cultivate slope with horse

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A farmer works a hillside using a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is usually a noun; OED records a rare old verb sense, to till.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare old verb sense meaning to till or work soil, related to till.

clue.text: Dare America to ruin this special relationship?

indicators.note: to ruin means the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A challenge to the USA to wreck the Anglo-American special relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Comradely friendship and trust between allies is what a special relationship ought to have.

clue.text: Approval for a time in warm clothing to burn?

indicators.note: approval for a time says one stands in place of the other inside the coat

parts.note: A plus T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Wearing a warm coat for a while gets approval, though it may make you burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps OK in where AT stood in OVERCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking food too long until it chars is the sense; a dish left too long will burn.

clue.text: Stick to tragedy? That's ridiculous

definitions.meaning: a cryptic request to an actor or writer: keep me away from comedy
an exclamation dismissing a suggestion as absurd

explanation.surface: Advice to a performer to play only tragic parts, met with scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a scornful retort meaning an idea is absurd, and literally asks not to be amused.

clue.text: … fine school, missing my appearance

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: missing says the following word is dropped from the school word

explanation.surface: Continuing the truant's tale: a fine school, but he never shows his face there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' is the deletion indicator; the ellipsis carries on the story from 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is an outward show or front, a false outward look someone presents.

clue.text: Too easy, one length in front

indicators.note: in places one and length within the front word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A race won too easily, one length ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib or superficially simple, achieved without effort, is the sense here.

clue.text: Tory trick

definitions.meaning: short for Conservative, a member of the British right-wing party

explanation.definitionFit: It abbreviates Conservative, and as a verb or noun it means a swindle.

clue.text: Size of boarding house at first obscured by dark

indicators.note: by means the shortened boarding house sits beside the dark word
at first obscured means the opening letter is hidden away

parts.note: a pension is a continental boarding house

explanation.surface: A boarding house's size is hidden by darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Measurement of length, breadth or extent of something is its size.

clue.text: So Christmas pudding may appear following meat course at last

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: at last picks out only the final letter of the word course

explanation.surface: Dinner service: after the meat course, the Christmas pudding finally arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas pudding is traditionally served doused in brandy and set alight, that is flambéed.

clue.text: Prisoner's alias?

parts.note: the nick is British slang for prison, so a prisoner's name could whimsically be the name in the nick

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the nick is a prison or police station, which gives the clue its second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed or familiar name, and a familiar name given in place of the real one is this.

clue.text: God! Writer has lost one lot of gold

indicators.note: has lost says something is removed from the word for a writer

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold; or, heraldic gold, is the other lot left behind

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise on hearing that an author has lost some gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God!' looks like an exclamation but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse mythology's hammer-wielding thunder deity carries this name.

clue.text: Quietly happy remark: there's room for me

indicators.note: room for me says one word stands in place of the other within the remark

explanation.surface: Someone happily remarks that there is space for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts PLACE where ME stood in COMMENT, giving COM-PLACE-NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smugly self-satisfied is a quiet kind of contentment with one's lot.

clue.text: Secures dwarf that sewer may employ

parts.note: titch is British slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a little man, with a drain hinted at by sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain but means one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A looped embroidery stitch like a row of links is something a needleworker uses.

clue.text: Is likely to be effective, we hear, as school subject

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said aloud, matching a different spelling

parts.note: would work means is likely to be effective

explanation.surface: Someone judges which subject at school would prove a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry taught as a craft lesson in British schools went by this name.

clue.text: Timely drink in old Indian city

indicators.note: in places the drink within the city name

explanation.surface: A well-timed drink in a historic Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-timed, coming at a convenient moment, is the sense of the word.

clue.text: Khrushchev losing it on the way back, it's related

indicators.note: on the way back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
losing says the next word is taken out of the first name

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader loses something on his return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing it' turns NIKITA into NIKA, which 'on the way back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of the same family or similar in kind is the sense of this word.

clue.text: Temporary pole army just fixed

indicators.note: fixed means the letters are rigged into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers have just put up a makeshift pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift mast rigged at sea after the original is lost is called this.

clue.text: Pole virtually redundant

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A Polish worker is almost made redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is the definition, a stout pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, as used for a ship's mast or boom.

clue.text: Weeds are universal in the early hours

indicators.note: in places the universal letter within the early hours word

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Weeds spring up everywhere at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeds' are widow's weeds, black clothes worn in grief, not garden plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Widow's weeds are the black clothes worn in grief, so weeds can mean grief dress.

clue.text: Turn hastily away from wife, to hand drinks round

indicators.note: round means the serving word goes around the wife letter

parts.note: to serve is to hand drinks

explanation.surface: A man dodges his wife while pouring a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks round' suggests buying a round; 'round' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer sharply to avoid something is to change direction suddenly.

clue.text: Favouring country sports in spring, energy bursting all around

indicators.note: all around means the rearranged letters wrap round the spring word
bursting means the letters of energy are blown apart and reformed

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone keen on hunting and shooting is full of energy in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' is the anagram indicator and 'all around' the container. The green welly brigade are well-off British country folk in green rubber boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Green rubber boots are emblematic of the upper-class British rural set who hunt, shoot and fish.

clue.text: Shortly pack basic food for the tropics

indicators.note: shortly means the card word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a tarot is a pack of fortune-telling cards

explanation.surface: Packing staple provisions quickly for a trip to the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy tuber is a staple crop across tropical regions, eaten much like potato.

clue.text: Inhabitant of Tower fearing to be executed

indicators.note: to be executed means beheaded, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A prisoner in the Tower of London dreads his execution.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of London famously keeps black birds; legend says the kingdom falls if they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Large black birds are kept at the Tower of London, so one counts as a resident there.

clue.text: Crime nearly pinned on psychoanalyst, one hard to get on top of

definitions.text: one hard to get on top of

indicators.note: pinned on means the shortened crime is attached after the psychoanalyst
nearly means the crime word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A crime is almost blamed on a psychoanalyst who is hard to pin down.
explanation.definitionFit: A high Swiss Alpine peak in the Bernese Oberland is difficult to climb to the summit of.

clue.text: Corporation is good for Berlin

definitions.meaning: a corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly
the German word for good, as spoken in Berlin

explanation.surface: A company is a good thing for the German capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation is jokingly a paunch, a belly; and the German for good is the same letters.

clue.text: Near end of play perhaps, finally lose voice

parts.note: Act IV comes near the end of a five-act play

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of lose

explanation.surface: Late in a performance, an actor finally loses his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' is the grammatical sense: verbs have active and passive voices.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a verb's voice is either this one, where the subject acts, or passive.

clue.text: Prepare to sleep in wooden seat

definitions.meaning: to ... down for the night, getting ready to drop off
a long high-backed wooden bench with arms

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to nod off in a wooden chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make oneself comfortable for rest; the noun is a high-backed wooden bench.

clue.text: Not liking to catch companion breaking eggs

indicators.note: to catch means the dislike word holds the companion letters inside it

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes cooking gets a friend to crack the eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking eggs' suggests cooking; it is chicks emerging from shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicks emerging by cracking their shells from within is this process.
